source: DualSPHysics v5.4 (commit ef3721a; Dominguez et al. 2022), pySurf's reference run, written, run and measured with pySurf's breaking tracker by dualSphysics/tools/mostertRuns.py (in the repository's history to commit 27c0a03), recorded 2026-11-10. A cross-check: it validates neither code.
case: Mostert and Deike's (2020) H0/h0 = 0.3 on a 3 degree beach, 2D: a wave run and a still-water run of the same tank, energies summed over the fluid, the share lost in active breaking, 32 ppd, artificial viscosity
note: Times in seconds from the crest's passage of the tuning gauge, as pySurf's count from its starting crest; h0 = 1 m. runWall is the solver's wall time in seconds; fluidParticles and wallClockSeconds in the summary fields are placeholders.
